findings.message: Scope in says only `squatch/scorecard.py`, `tests/test_scorecard.py`, and `tests/test_seeded_phase5_02.py` are sibling-new in this admission and are never Context. Section 20 gives that set for the `phase5-continue` admission. This ticket depends on `scorecard-reporting`, so `squatch/scorecard.py` and `tests/test_scorecard.py` are already merged when it runs. `status-projection` must fence the merged scorecard seams/tests and embed them as existing Context (or name them as measured on-demand exceptions). The ticket as written would forbid that. It also never names the real sibling-new paths of this admission: `tests/test_status.py`, `squatch/baseline.py`, `tests/test_baseline.py`, and `tests/test_seeded_phase5_03.py`.
findings.paved_road: Replace the sibling-new sentence with the set for this admission: `tests/test_status.py`, `squatch/baseline.py`, `tests/test_baseline.py`, and `tests/test_seeded_phase5_03.py`. State that merged `squatch/scorecard.py` and `tests/test_scorecard.py` are existing Context for `status-projection`, pinned at authoring-time sizes or named as measured on-demand exceptions. Add a criterion that `tests/test_seeded_phase5_02.py` pins that partition.

findings.message: The acceptance criteria never require a max-effort synthetic render within `REQ_RENDER_HEADROOM` for the authored seeds. They also never require every existing fence path to be embedded Context or an individually named measured on-demand exception. The embedded continuation pattern (`test_authoring_sizes_and_max_effort_render_headroom`, `test_context_closure_predecessor_preservation_and_sibling_exclusion`) and section 20's Phase 5 rule both require this. Without it, `status-projection` or `baseline-binding-reader` could be authored in a form that cannot render.
findings.paved_road: Add criteria that `tests/test_seeded_phase5_02.py` pins authoring-time Context sizes as synthetic fixtures and proves a max-effort `specs/implement.md` render of each authored seed is within `RENDER_BOUND_CHARS['max'] * REQ_RENDER_HEADROOM`. The test must also assert that each existing fence path is embedded Context or a named on-demand exception, following `tests/test_seeded_phase4_05.py`.

findings.message: `baseline-binding-reader` ownership is given only as 'the machine-ticket starting-state caller named by its requisition'. This continuation is that requisition's author, so it must resolve that caller to a concrete path. Otherwise the seeded test cannot pin the exact fence the criteria require.
findings.paved_road: Name the concrete starting-state caller path in Scope in, for example `squatch/policy.py` (owner of `policy.starting_state`), together with its focused test. Pin that exact fence in `tests/test_seeded_phase5_02.py`.
